_readme: status 'accepted' = verified as intentional; it stays out of the way.
status 'pending'  = real debt, still open. Also quiet — the gate is on NEW findings.
A finding missing from this file fails the run, so growth is loud while the backlog is not.
Remove an entry once the finding stops occurring; the checker reports stale entries too.
The 2026-07-25 pass took this from 58 findings to 18. Everything structural is gone:
0 import cycles in src/shared, 0 layer violations, 0 dead IPC channels, 0 orphaned
modules that were not deliberate, and every storage key and duplicated export that
had two owners now has one. What remains is 14 accepted entries and 3 pending ones,
and all 3 are the same honest shape: a pure layer that is built and tested but has
no consumer yet, which its own phase report already records as its boundary.

duplicate-export:canUndo.note: Two unrelated undo stacks (renderer action history, CSV editor). Same verb, different domain — not shared logic.

duplicate-export:clearAll.note: Generic store verb on two unrelated stores (clipboard history, notifications).

duplicate-export:LANG_LABELS.note: TranslateContent's list is translation *target* languages; i18n/core's is UI languages. Deliberately independent — CLAUDE.md keeps those two selectors separate.

duplicate-export:pushHistory.note: Two unrelated history stacks, same verb — as canUndo.

duplicate-export:THEMES.note: readerSettings' THEMES is reader typography themes; theme.ts's is app colour themes. Different things, similarly named.

duplicate-export:qbitTransfers.note: main/scraper/qbittorrent.ts is the real WebUI call; scraper/data/fixtures.ts is the sample-data generator the mock port still uses for profiles with no client configured. Same noun, opposite sides of the port boundary — main may not import the renderer.

duplicate-export:translate.note: renderer/translator.ts translates study text; i18n/core.ts translates UI chrome. Unrelated by design.

duplicate-storage:jp-booted.note: One writer (App.tsx), one reader (BootScreen). Handoff, not co-ownership.

duplicate-storage:jp-os-personalization-.note: customCss.ts reads osPersonalization's blob only to honour the customCssEnabled gate at boot; documented inside bootCustomCss().

duplicate-storage:jp-user-css.note: This is the <style> element id, shared by the module that creates it and the one that removes it on reset. Not a storage key — it matches the jp- convention by coincidence.

orphan-module:src/renderer/motion/index..note: Barrel for the motion framework; consumers import the leaf modules directly. It costs nothing and is the documented public face of that folder.

test-only-module:src/renderer/data/media.note: Named 'fixtures'. Test data is meant to be test-only.

test-only-module:src/shared/i18n/catalog.note: CLAUDE.md says so explicitly: 'for tooling and tests only; importing it from app code puts every language back in the bundle'.

test-only-module:src/renderer/theme/toke.note: The typed mirror of tokens.css and the source THEME_TOKEN_REFERENCE.md is generated from; PHASE_1_IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md and UI_UX_CORE_SHELL_EXECUTION_PLAN.md §12 both say to keep it in sync. It was an orphan — nothing read it, so nothing noticed drift. renderer/__tests__/themeTokenMirror.test.ts now checks every mirrored token against the CSS, which is why it reads as test-only: the test is the consumer, deliberately.

test-only-module:src/shared/episodeProce.note: §1 episode processing: built and tested, no consumer. The settings UI edits the rules; nothing applies them, because no connector exists to apply them to. Matches the boundary §1/§2 state honestly.

test-only-module:src/shared/mediaProvide.note: §7 sync journal, built and tested, no consumer. The original note blamed 'provider execution is out of scope', but provider execution now exists (Jikan/AniList metadata, Jimaku/OpenSubtitles subtitles). The real reason is different: this is a cross-device sync-envelope subsystem, and the app has no cross-device sync at all — no deviceId, no sync surface, no consumer for mediaProviderSyncPersistence or Resolution either. Wiring it would mean inventing that feature and adding a write path nothing reads. Left intact as designed, unfinished work.

test-only-module:src/shared/mediaWorkspa.note: ADR-003's exit gate. The allowlist must be empty and the adopted-surface list is what mediaWorkspaceI18n.test.ts parses — a gate whose only consumer is its own test is the point, not an accident.

test-only-module:src/main/dictionary/imp.note: A process entry point, not a library. Its real caller is utilityProcess.fork() in importIpc.ts, which names it by built path ('.vite/build/importWorker.js' via importJobs.dictionaryImportWorkerPath) — a runtime string the static import graph cannot follow, exactly like src/main.ts and src/preload.ts. forge.config.ts builds it as a third Vite target, so a broken entry fails the build rather than going unnoticed. The test import is of runDictionaryImport/attachDictionaryImportWorker, the two halves that are testable without a child process.

test-only-module:src/shared/subtitleFusi.note: The EN→JA fusion plan's F7 ship gate. Its real consumer is tools/fusion-eval.cjs, which esbuild-bundles this file at run time by path — the same kind of runtime reference the static import graph cannot follow as importWorker.ts, and the same pattern tools/grammar-audit.cjs and tools/i18n-check.cjs already use. It is deliberately not imported by the app: the harness scores the pipeline from outside it, needs real media and the Whisper runtime, and must not become something product code can call. If tools/fusion-eval.cjs is ever deleted, this becomes a genuine orphan and should be deleted with it.

test-only-module:src/renderer/components.note: L2 primitive layer, landed ahead of its consumer on purpose. LIQUID_WORKPLACE_TRANSFORMATION_PLAN.md L2 ships tokens and primitives BEFORE any surface migrates, so the Files app and the Video pilot are built in the Liquid language rather than retrofitted into it. Its stylesheet IS imported by renderer/main.tsx; only the React component has no app-side caller yet. Closes when L4 migrates the Video player. src/.coordination/liquid-workplace/L2_PRIMITIVES.md records the boundary.
Same L2 boundary as LiquidSurface.tsx: the scaffold spine exists so a migrating app has a destination, and no app has migrated yet. Closes when L4 migrates the Video player.

Same L2 boundary as LiquidAppScaffold.tsx. The dock is the compact-width home for the rail's routes, which the scaffold drops below its `medium` breakpoint; it and AdaptiveRail/ContextToolbar (reachable through it) complete §5.2's primitive list. No app has migrated, so nothing imports it yet. Closes when L4 migrates the Video player.

Same L2 boundary as LiquidAppScaffold.tsx. Fills the scaffold's inspector slot and carries the required close path (control, Escape, caller state) plus focus return. No app has migrated, so nothing imports it yet. Closes when L4 migrates the Video player.
